title: Resolve a bare herding run's agent through the generation tier slot
action: herding-bare-agent D1-D5. Today `resolve_agent_command(cfg, agent)` (wave.rs, around line 305) resolves in three steps: an explicit `agent` name through the registry, then a string-valued `herding.agent_command` through the registry, then the array split with the built-in default. A configured cell-execution tier slot is invisible to it, so a bare `bee herding run` opened claude-sonnet while `models.claude.generation` named agy-flash. Insert ONE step between the explicit-name lookup and the `herding.agent_command` lookup: read `cfg.models.<runtime>.generation`; when and only when it is an object with `kind == "herding"` AND a non-empty string `agent`, resolve that name through `resolve_from_registry` (the same path `--agent` takes, so an unknown name returns AgentCommandError::UnknownAgent listing every registry key — never a silent fallback, D4). Every other slot shape — kind herding with no agent, a plain model-name string, kind cli, null, absent, a non-object — is skipped and resolution continues to `herding.agent_command` exactly as today (D2). `<runtime>` is the value of the `BEE_RUNTIME` env var when it names claude, codex, or opencode, else `claude` (D3) — the same unknown-runtime fallback `verbs/drivers/models.rs` resolve_tier already applies; add no new flag and change no call site (cfg is already the whole config document, and `bee herding wave`'s `resolve_agent_command(cfg, None)` call inherits the new step for free, D5). The resolver returns a TRIPLE (kind, args, env) — the registry entry's env map (defaults-and-agent-env D4) — so the new branch must return `resolve_from_registry`'s env intact, never an empty map. Keep the existing doc comment block on the function truthful: it currently enumerates the three reference spellings from herd-registry D2 — extend that enumeration with the slot step and its precedence position. Add unit tests beside the existing resolver tests in this file, covering: (a) the slot wins over a differing `herding.agent_command`; (b) an explicit `--agent`-style name still wins over the slot; (c) kind-herding-without-agent, a plain model-name slot, and a kind-cli slot each fall through to `agent_command` unchanged; (d) a slot naming an agent absent from `herding.agents` returns UnknownAgent, not the agent_command value; (e) a slot resolving to an object-shaped registry entry carries that entry's env through; (f) with BEE_RUNTIME unset the claude block is read (guard any env-dependent test against cross-test interference — prefer a pure helper taking the runtime name, with a thin env-reading wrapper, over setting env inside a test). SEQUENCING: herding-worker-standalone landed on main (commit 8fbc64dc). Do NOT start until herding-limit-pause has also landed; rebase the worktree onto main first and re-read the live function before editing — RealHerdr::pane_run is now a raw Command (no call() JSON) after hlp-0.

truths: Precedence is exactly: explicit agent name, then a herd generation slot naming an agent, then herding.agent_command, then the built-in default array
Only {kind:"herding", agent:"<non-empty>"} participates; every other slot shape falls through unchanged
A slot agent missing from herding.agents fails closed with UnknownAgent listing the known keys
The runtime block is BEE_RUNTIME when it names a known runtime, else claude; no new CLI flag and no call-site change
The new branch returns the registry entry's env map intact (defaults-and-agent-env D4) — the slot path carries env exactly as the --agent path does
The resolver's doc comment enumerates the new step in its precedence position
